passages.title: The Cup Final
passages.passage: Last Saturday our school football team played in the final of the district cup for the first time (1)____ ten years. The match was held at the stadium in the town centre, and the stands were full (2)____ students. My brother Nam is the goalkeeper, so my whole family sat in the front row with a banner that my mother had painted the night before. The first half was very slow. Both teams were nervous, and there were hardly (3)____ chances for either side. Then, just before the break, our captain scored (4)____ a corner and the crowd went wild. In the second half the other team attacked without stopping. Nam made three great saves. (5)____, with only ten minutes left, a striker finally got the ball past him. One-one. I could hardly watch. The referee had already looked at his watch (6)____ our youngest player, who is only in grade 7, picked up a loose ball near the halfway line. He ran past two defenders and shot from a long way out. The ball hit the post, rolled along the line and went in. Nobody could believe (7)____ had happened. When the final whistle blew, the players lifted the boy onto their shoulders and carried him round the pitch. My brother admitted later that he (8)____ never been so tired in his life. On the way home Dad said that if the boy (9)____ training, he could play for the city one day. I am not sure about that, but I know I will remember that afternoon (10)____ the rest of my life.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After for the first time we say in + a period: for the first time in ten years. For ten years describes how long something lasts, which is not the meaning here.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The adjective full takes of: full of students. Filled with and packed with exist, but full with does not.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Hardly any means almost none. Hardly is already negative, so hardly no is a double negative, and hardly some / hardly few are not English.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: In football you score from a corner, a free kick or a penalty, meaning the goal came out of that situation. By would introduce the scorer, not the move.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The goalkeeper made great saves, but then a goal was scored against him: a contrast, so However. Therefore gives a result and Moreover adds a similar point, which the sentence is not.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Had already looked at his watch + when + past simple describes a sudden event that interrupts a situation. While needs a continuing action, and until would mean he stopped looking at that moment.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The clause needs a subject: what had happened = the thing that had happened. That cannot be the subject of had happened, and which needs a noun before it.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb (admitted) the present perfect moves back to the past perfect: had never been. Has keeps the original tense and was never been is not a tense at all.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Dad's actual words were If he keeps training, he can play for the city. After the past reporting verb said, the whole conditional moves one tense back: keeps becomes kept and can becomes could. Keep has no -s for the singular subject the boy, and will / would keep never go inside the if-clause.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: For the rest of my life is a fixed expression of duration with for. During is possible with some periods but never with the rest of my life, and since needs a starting point.

passages.title: Six O'Clock at the Market
passages.passage: My grandmother has sold vegetables at the same market for nearly forty years, and last Sunday she let me help her (1)____ the first time. We left the house while it was still dark. (2)____ the time we reached the market, the lorries from the countryside had already arrived and men were carrying boxes of cabbages on their shoulders. Grandma greeted everyone (3)____ name. She has known most of the other sellers since they were children, and they clearly respect her. My job was simple: I had to arrange the tomatoes in neat rows (4)____ the best ones were at the front. By seven the first customers appeared. (5)____ of them were mothers who wanted to finish their shopping before work. One woman argued about the price for nearly five minutes, but Grandma just smiled and gave her an extra chilli. "If you (6)____ her leave unhappy, she won't come back," she told me afterwards. At nine o'clock a boy on a motorbike delivered a basket of fresh herbs (7)____ smell filled the whole corner. I had never noticed how loud a market is: bells, radios, people calling out prices, and somewhere a rooster that would not stop. By eleven there was hardly (8)____ left on the table, and my feet hurt so much that I could barely stand. Grandma, (9)____ is seventy-two, did not look tired at all. She counted the money, gave me a note for my help and said I could come again (10)____ I promised not to eat the strawberries next time.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is for the first time. At first exists but is not followed by time, and in and on do not collocate with the first time.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: By the time + clause means not later than the moment when, and it explains the past perfect had already arrived. At the time means at that moment and is not followed by a clause with reached.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: To greet or call somebody by name is the fixed expression. With, in and on never combine with name in this sense.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The second clause gives the purpose of arranging the rows, so so that is needed. In order requires to + verb or that, and as if and even though change the meaning.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Most of them = the majority. Almost is an adverb and needs all (almost all of them); much is for uncountable nouns, and every is never followed by of.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Only let is followed by object + bare infinitive: let her leave. Allow, permit and get need to: allow her to leave.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The smell belongs to the herbs, so the possessive relative whose is needed before the noun smell. Which and that cannot stand directly before a noun in this way.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Hardly anything means almost nothing. Hardly is already negative, so hardly nothing is a double negative, and something / everything do not follow hardly.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Extra information about a person between commas takes who. That is not used in a non-defining clause, which is for things, and whom is only an object.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: As long as = on condition that: she can come again if she promises. Unless would mean the opposite, and in case introduces a precaution, not a condition.

passages.title: Boxes Everywhere
passages.passage: We moved house in July, and I still have not (1)____ used to the new flat. For twelve years I had lived in the same room, with the same view of the same mango tree, and I did not want to leave. My parents, (2)____, were excited. The new place is closer to their offices and has a lift, which matters (3)____ my grandfather cannot manage stairs any more. The packing took two whole weeks. Mum wrote the name of a room on every box, but by the end nobody was paying attention, and the kitchen knives ended (4)____ in a box marked 'bathroom'. On moving day the lorry arrived an hour late, and the driver refused to carry the piano (5)____ we paid him extra. My father was furious, but there was nothing he could do. The strangest moment came when the old flat was completely empty. Our voices sounded different, and the walls had pale squares (6)____ the pictures used to hang. I took one last photo and closed the door. Since then I have slowly been getting to know the neighbourhood. There is a bakery downstairs, a park (7)____ five minutes' walk of our building, and a boy next door who plays the same online game as me. Last week I finally (8)____ round to unpacking my books, and the room started to feel like mine. My old friends have promised to visit, though I know that promises like that are not always (9)____. Still, Mum says that by next summer I will wonder (10)____ I ever made such a fuss.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Get used to something means become familiar with it, so the past participle got completes have not got used to. Take, make and put do not combine with used to.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The parents feel the opposite of the writer, and the word sits between commas as an adverb: however. Although and despite must begin a clause or phrase, not stand alone between commas.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The grandfather's difficulty with stairs is the reason the lift matters, so because. So would make it a result, and although would make the two facts contrast, which they do not.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: End up + place means finish in that place, usually by accident. End out, end off and end over are not phrasal verbs.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The driver would only carry the piano on the condition of extra money: refused … unless we paid = except if we paid. If we paid would mean he refused because of the payment, the opposite of the sense.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The clause tells us the place the pictures used to hang, so the relative adverb where is needed. Which and that would need to be the subject or object of hang, and when refers to time.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Within + distance + of a place means no further than that: within five minutes' walk of our building. Inside is for enclosed spaces, and among and along do not describe distance.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Get round to doing something means finally find the time to do it. Come round means visit or wake up, and go round and turn round do not take to + -ing.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A promise is kept or broken; here it is passive, so the past participle. Made collocates with promise but means giving the promise, not carrying it out, and held and done do not collocate.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The writer will ask himself the reason for his behaviour: wonder why I made such a fuss. If would question whether the fuss happened at all, which he already knows, and that and what cannot introduce this clause.

passages.title: Paper Wings
passages.passage: Every March the wind along the coast becomes strong and steady, and that is when the kite competition (1)____ place. Anyone can enter, as (2)____ as the kite is made by hand. This year my cousin Bao and I decided to build one together. We spent three weekends in his garage cutting bamboo and gluing paper, and we argued (3)____ the colours the whole time. In the end we painted it red and gold, (4)____ are the colours of our school. On the morning of the contest (5)____ were more than two hundred kites lying on the sand, and the beach was full of families, dogs and food sellers. The judges give points for beauty, for height and for how long a kite stays (6)____ the air. Our first flight was a disaster. The string broke after twenty seconds and the kite landed in the sea. Bao wanted to give (7)____, but an old man who had been watching came over and showed us how to tie the string properly. On our second try the kite rose slowly, then caught the wind and climbed higher (8)____ almost every other kite on the beach. It stayed there for nearly an hour. We did not win first prize, (9)____ we did get a certificate for the most beautiful kite. Bao has already started drawing plans for next year, and this time we are going to test the string (10)____ we go anywhere near the water.

questions.q: Blank (1): write one word.
questions.explanation: An event takes place = happens; the present simple fits a yearly routine. Has place and makes place are not English, and took would break the present-tense description.

questions.q: Blank (2): write one word.
questions.explanation: As long as = on condition that; as far as is also accepted here in the sense of to the extent that. As soon as would be about time, not a rule, and if cannot sit between as … as.

questions.q: Blank (3): write one word.
questions.explanation: You argue about (or over) a subject. Argue for means support a side, and argue with needs a person, not the colours.

questions.q: Blank (4): write one word.
questions.explanation: A non-defining relative clause after a comma, referring to things (the colours), takes which. That is not used after a comma in this kind of clause, and they would need a new sentence.

questions.q: Blank (5): write one word.
questions.explanation: There were + plural noun introduces the existence of something, and the verb were shows this. They would need an earlier noun to refer to, and it is singular.

questions.q: Blank (6): write one word.
questions.explanation: A kite or plane stays in the air. On the air is used for radio and television, and up cannot be followed by the air here.

questions.q: Blank (7): write one word.
questions.explanation: Give up = stop trying; give in = stop resisting and accept defeat, also acceptable after a failure. Give away means hand something to someone else, and give out means distribute or stop working.

questions.q: Blank (8): write one word.
questions.explanation: A comparative (higher) is completed by than. Then is a time word and a common spelling trap, and as only pairs with as high as.

questions.q: Blank (9): write one word.
questions.explanation: The two halves contrast, so a contrast linker: but, or although / though / yet. And does not signal the contrast, and however cannot join two clauses after a comma without a full stop or semicolon.

questions.q: Blank (10): write one word.
questions.explanation: The lesson of the story is to check the string first, so before we go near the water. After would repeat the mistake, and until would mean they keep testing while going towards the sea.
